questions.prompt: On what occasions should we be polite?

answers.basic: It matters when you're asking someone for help or sharing a space with strangers. For example, I'd keep my voice down when taking a call on the subway. Small things like that make it easier for everyone to share a crowded place without getting irritated with each other.

questions.prompt: What did you do to show your politeness as a child?

answers.basic: I used to greet relatives when they came over and thank them if they brought something. My family would remind me if I forgot. I wanted the adults to feel welcome, so I'd sometimes bring them a chair or get them some water as well.

questions.prompt: Do you think being polite is very important?

answers.basic: Yes. A polite request usually makes it easier for both people to deal with a problem. That matters when you're busy or when you disagree. Even at work, asking someone to check one specific thing politely can make a difficult conversation go much more smoothly.

questions.prompt: How did you learn to be polite as a child?

answers.basic: I mostly learned from watching my family. They would say thank you to the people who helped them, and I gradually started doing the same. I remember being reminded to wait until someone had finished speaking before I jumped in with my own story.
